summary: The fixes are real, not cosmetic. Every new count re-derives from the raw logs, the two claims that were reversed were reversed on evidence with a proper discriminating control, and the two hardest items — C13 and C21 — were settled by measurement on the exact structure they concern rather than hedged. I verified the delegate probes structurally (parent_tool_use_id on every tool_use), not just by reading the final string, because 'the delegate reported its own effort' is precisely the claim a parent-executed printenv would fake. It did not fake it. One correction, C4, regressed while being fixed: the session matrix's env row lost its honest '(earlier run)' tag and gained a '2/2' that comes from delegate-scoped runs, so a session-level cell is now backed by a sub-agent measurement. Two bookkeeping items and one .gitignore side effect round it out.

findings.was: 'CLAUDE_EFFORT does not report a delegate's level' was asserted with no run behind it — every printenv in the evidence set executed in the main thread, and the supporting token-spend oracle is one the same file deprecates.
findings.verdict_direction: reversed, correctly — the old claim is refuted and the new opposite claim is properly measured
findings.checked: STRUCTURAL VERIFICATION, not string reading. In fm-probehigh-1 and fm-probe-1 I traced parent_tool_use_id on every tool_use: the Agent call has parent=null, and BOTH the Bash (printenv CLAUDE_EFFORT) and the WebSearch carry parent=<the Agent tool_use id> — they executed inside the delegate. This is the check that matters, because a parent-executed printenv would produce a plausible-looking MYEFFORT line that means nothing. Results: fm-probehigh (effort: high, session xhigh) → MYEFFORT=high RESULTS=7, 2/2, zero rejections; fm-probe (nothing declared) → MYEFFORT=xhigh RESULTS=ERROR, 2/2, 400 quoting 'xhigh'. The discriminating cell is fm-probehigh reading `high` while its session ran `xhigh` — a value that cannot be the parent's. It also refutes the old wording on the exact configuration the old wording described ('inside a subagent pinned by frontmatter it read the parent's'). Both agents declare tools: WebSearch, Bash, so they could genuinely run it; both arms ran on claude-opus-5 only, ruling out a model swap.
findings.residual: none. Two oracles agree per run: the delegate's own printenv and the tier the 400 quotes.

findings.was: The built-in-delegate escape (Agent tool per-call `model` override) was prescribed but never measured.
findings.checked: pl-gpplain-1/2: subagent_type=general-purpose spawned plainly from an --effort xhigh session → SUB=RESULTS=ERROR 2/2, 400 quoting 'xhigh', stream shows claude-opus-5 only. pl-gpsonnet-1/2: same session, model override on the Agent call → SUB=RESULTS=7 2/2, zero rejections, stream carries both 'sonnet' (the call parameter) and 'claude-sonnet-5' (the resolved model), confirming the override actually resolved rather than being silently dropped. Clean two-armed contrast with the model control present in both arms.
findings.residual: The Agent tool's own carve-out — 'Ignored for subagent_type: "fork" — forks always inherit the parent model' — is still unmentioned. Not an over-claim any more, because the sentence is now scoped to `general-purpose` specifically rather than to built-in delegates generally. Informational only.

findings.was: The shipped change put effort: xhigh in PLUGIN agent frontmatter, a load path never measured.
findings.checked: pl-pluginprobe-1/2: subagent_type=`claude-code-harness:tmp-plugin-probe` — the plugin namespace prefix proves it resolved through the plugin loader, not as a project agent. From an --effort xhigh session it searched 2/2 (RESULTS=7, zero rejections) on claude-opus-5.
findings.adversarial_note: There is no negative control on the plugin path (no plugin agent declaring nothing). The inference is nonetheless forced rather than assumed: the delegate ran on claude-opus-5 in an xhigh session, and the only established way for that combination to search is to be at high or below — which on this agent can only have come from its frontmatter effort:. If the plugin loader had dropped the key it would have inherited xhigh and failed, exactly as fm-plain and ag-plain do. Accepting as closed.

issues_introduced.location: native-capabilities.md, session matrix row 6: `| xhigh | CLAUDE_CODE_EFFORT_LEVEL (env) | fails 2/2 |`
issues_introduced.problem: This row previously read 'fails 5/5 (earlier run)' — an honest provenance tag on a number from the disavowed matrix. v1.19.5 replaced it with a bare '2/2' that reads as one of the re-measured session rows. It is not. No run in the evidence set has an env-pinned session call WebSearch itself with the good oracle.
issues_introduced.how_i_verified: parent_tool_use_id tracing. In out-base-1.jsonl (a genuine session row) the WebSearch tool_use has parent=null — the session called it. In the only two env runs that produce a 400 (agenv-envhigh-1 and ctl-fmenvhigh-1) the WebSearch tool_use has parent=<the Agent tool_use id> — it ran inside a delegate. Every env run in the scratchpad is driven by a prompt that explicitly forbids the parent from searching ('Сам WebSearch не вызывай'), so a session-level env measurement structurally cannot exist in this batch.
issues_introduced.why_it_matters: The other five rows of that table are 'a session raised its level this way and searched'. Row 6 is now 'a delegate whose declared effort: high was overridden by env searched and failed'. The underlying physics is not in dispute — env pins xhigh, xhigh fails — but the cell asserts a measurement class it does not have, and it does so in the one table the release rewrote to stop doing exactly that. The pre-fix wording was more honest than the post-fix wording.
issues_introduced.correction: Either (a) qualify: 'fails 2/2 — measured on a delegate sub-request under an env-pinned session; the session's own search under env was not re-measured with this oracle', or (b) run it: run.sh with CLAUDE_CODE_EFFORT_LEVEL=xhigh and the original prompt.txt, 2 runs, ~2 minutes. Option (b) is cheap and makes the row genuinely homogeneous with its neighbours.

issues_introduced.problem: The un-ignore is directory-wide, so three pre-existing local audit directories that were previously invisible now surface as untracked in a public repo: .claude/audits/config-dir-portability/, consumer-journey-v1-16-0/, session-context-hook/ (confirmed via git check-ignore: all three now NOT ignored). The file's own header states 'Nothing runtime, local, or personal should ever land here.'
issues_introduced.why_it_matters: Bounded — release.sh stages a curated surface — but a human `git add -A` now sweeps whatever local audit material happens to be on disk into a public marketplace repo. The whitelist existed to make that impossible.
issues_introduced.correction: Either commit the three deliberately (if they belong) or narrow the rule to the audit dirs actually intended for the repo. A one-line alternative that preserves the whitelist's guarantee: keep `!/.claude/audits/` but add `/.claude/audits/*/` + `!/.claude/audits/*/AUDIT-*.json`, so only verdict artifacts are trackable.
